questions.tutor: A symmetric matrix satisfies A = Aᵀ, meaning element aᵢⱼ = aⱼᵢ for all i, j.

questions.question: What is the inverse of matrix A = [[2, 1], [5, 3]]?
If A is a 3×4 matrix and B is a 4×2 matrix, what is the size of the product AB?
questions.tutor: Matrix multiplication: (m×n)(n×p) = m×p. So (3×4)(4×2) = 3×2.

questions.question: What is the trace of matrix [[4, 2, 1], [3, 5, 0], [1, 2, 6]]?
questions.tutor: The trace is the sum of diagonal elements: 4 + 5 + 6 = 15.

questions.question: A square matrix with all elements above the main diagonal equal to zero is called:
questions.tutor: A lower triangular matrix has all elements above the main diagonal equal to zero.

questions.question: What is the rank of matrix [[1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6], [7, 8, 9]]?
questions.tutor: Row reducing reveals only 2 linearly independent rows (R3 = 2R2 - R1), so rank = 2.

questions.question: Given A = [[1, 0], [0, 1]] and B = [[3, 4], [5, 6]], what is AB?
questions.tutor: Multiplying any matrix by the identity matrix I returns the same matrix: IA = AI = A.

questions.question: What is the determinant of a 3×3 matrix [[1,2,3],[0,4,5],[0,0,6]]?
questions.tutor: For an upper triangular matrix, det = product of diagonal elements = 1×4×6 = 24.

questions.question: Which of the following conditions makes a matrix singular?
questions.tutor: A singular matrix has determinant = 0, meaning it has no inverse.

The cofactor of element a₁₂ in matrix [[1,2,3],[4,5,6],[7,8,9]] is:
If A = [[2, 3], [1, 4]] and B = [[1, 0], [2, 1]], what is A + B?
questions.tutor: Matrix addition is element-wise: [[2+1, 3+0], [1+2, 4+1]] = [[3,3],[3,5]].

questions.question: What is the transpose of matrix [[1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6]]?
questions.tutor: Transpose flips rows and columns: a 2×3 matrix becomes a 3×2 matrix.

questions.question: Using Gaussian elimination, solve: x + y = 4, 2x - y = 2. Find x.
questions.tutor: Adding the two equations: 3x = 6 → x = 2. Then y = 4 - 2 = 2.

questions.question: A matrix multiplied by its inverse gives:
questions.tutor: By definition, A × A⁻¹ = A⁻¹ × A = I, the identity matrix.

questions.question: What is the eigenvalue of matrix [[3, 1], [0, 3]]?
questions.tutor: det(A - λI) = (3-λ)² = 0 → λ = 3 (repeated eigenvalue).

questions.question: Which matrix operation is NOT generally commutative?
questions.tutor: Matrix multiplication is generally not commutative: AB ≠ BA in most cases.

questions.question: A 4×4 identity matrix has how many elements equal to 1?
questions.tutor: An n×n identity matrix has exactly n ones along the main diagonal. For 4×4, that is 4 ones.

questions.question: If det(A) = 5 and det(B) = 3, what is det(AB)?
questions.tutor: det(AB) = det(A) × det(B) = 5 × 3 = 15.
